_notes: Which file types the Source Library accepts, and why it refuses the rest.
Edit this file to change the policy - no code change is needed. The server
reads it on each request (cached on the file's mtime), and the browser reads
the same list from GET /api/v1/source-library/upload-policy, so the two
cannot drift apart.
Why refusing matters: a type the pipeline cannot read is not rejected
downstream, it is stored, listed as 'Processed', and silently contributes
nothing to any generation. 110 of AIM's 121 .doc files went in exactly that
way and nobody noticed for a month. A refusal costs the user one re-save.
supported_extensions: lowercase, no leading dot. Anything not listed here is
refused, so adding a new type is a deliberate act.
blocked_extensions: refused with this exact message. Use it for a type that
LOOKS supported but is not, so the user gets a reason instead of a generic
'unsupported' - each message should say what to do next.
2026-08-27: doc/ppt/xls are all pre-2007 OLE2 binaries. python-docx,
python-pptx and openpyxl read the modern OOXML containers only. .doc has an
antiword fallback and the binary is now in the DIS image, but it stays
blocked on purpose: antiword was shown to EXTRACT these files, which is not
the same as extracting them faithfully. Re-open .doc once someone has
compared its output against the originals - move it to supported_extensions.

blocked_extensions.doc: Legacy Word (.doc) is not accepted yet. Its text extraction has not been verified against the original documents, and an inaccurate extraction is worse than none - it reads as usable content. Re-save as .docx and upload that.
blocked_extensions.ppt: Legacy PowerPoint (.ppt) cannot be read - the extractor supports the modern .pptx container only, so the upload would produce no text at all. Re-save as .pptx and upload that.
blocked_extensions.xls: Legacy Excel (.xls) cannot be read - the extractor supports the modern .xlsx container only, so the upload would produce no text at all. Re-save as .xlsx and upload that.
